description:
Workspace-architectural feature request: expose a public test-harness module (gated behind feature='test-harness') for each *-server crate, exporting contract-compliance test suites parameterised over any backend implementation.

## Background

bd:JMAP-x2gd.45 (chat-server review) raised this for ChatBackend. The same shape applies to every backend trait in the workspace:
- MailBackend (jmap-mail-server)
- ChatBackend (jmap-chat-server)
- CalendarsBackend (jmap-calendars-server)
- TasksBackend (jmap-tasks-server)
- ContactsBackend (jmap-contacts-server)
- FileNodeBackend (jmap-filenode-server)
- SharingBackend (jmap-sharing-server)
- MetadataBackend (jmap-metadata-server)

Each trait has 10-20 methods. Implementing one correctly — particularly with the contract nuances flagged by review (per-target atomicity, state-token bump rules, memberCount invariants, expire_message idempotency, blob-not-found surface, etc.) — is a substantial undertaking. A downstream consumer writing their own backend (kith, stoa, third-party) has no way today to verify they got the contract right without running each crate's integration tests as a manual exercise.

## Proposed shape

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "test-harness")]
pub mod test_harness {
    /// Run the full ChatBackend contract suite against any backend.
    pub async fn run_contract_suite<B: ChatBackend>(backend: B);

    /// Run just the Space/set atomicity tests.
    pub async fn run_space_set_atomicity_suite<B: ChatBackend>(backend: B);

    /// Run just the invite-redemption tests.
    pub async fn run_invite_redemption_suite<B: ChatBackend>(backend: B);

    // ...
}
```

The kit's own integration tests would refactor to call `test_harness::run_*_suite(MemoryBackend::new()).await`. Third-party backends opt in by adding the same calls in their test suite. The feature gate keeps the test infrastructure out of production dep graphs.

## Why deferred

- Multi-bead epic across 8 *-server crates.
- Test infrastructure refactor is substantial (extracting tests/integration.rs into reusable suites).
- No external consumer demand signal yet — the kit's two known consumers (kith, stoa) share the maintainer, who has the integration test suite available.
- Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates', this should land on jmap-mail-server canonical first, then propagate to all 7 extension-server siblings in the same pass.

## Trigger to un-defer

- A third-party requests this on the issue tracker.
- A second internal consumer (calendars-client, tasks-client) ships and the maintainer wants to test against MemoryBackend conformance.
- A workspace-wide refactor of integration tests is planned for a different reason and this can ride along.

title: Deferred: workspace-wide test-harness public modules for all *-server backend traits
